Coevolutionary constraints of Zika virus nonstructural protein 5 replication and interferon antagonism activities
articles.abstract: Abstract The flavivirus nonstructural protein 5 performs multiple functions during infection, including RNA replication and type I interferon signaling antagonism. Although flavivirus NS5 proteins inhibit IFN signaling through distinct mechanisms, which suggests evolutionary flexibility, the evolutionary constraints for these activities to coexist within a single protein remain to be determined. Here, we map the Zika virus NS5 STAT2 antagonism determinants and compare them with replication constraints defined by deep mutational scanning. Antagonism and replication determinants extensively overlap, and no single amino acid substitution eliminates antagonism without impairing replication. Resolving these fitness landscapes in parallel identifies specific combinations of partially functional substitutions that retain replication capacity while markedly reducing antagonism. These viruses are profoundly attenuated in human STAT2 knock-in mice. Our results uncover a fundamental evolutionary constraint linking replication and immune evasion activities in NS5, highlight that STAT2 antagonism is essential for ZIKV pathogenesis and provide new avenues for attenuated ZIKV vaccines.

articles.title: Thrombin reshapes α-synuclein biochemical properties by N-terminal truncation
articles.abstract: Abstract Proteolytic processing of α-Synuclein (Syn) contributes to the molecular diversity and toxicity of its aggregates in Parkinson’s disease, yet the proteases responsible for disease-relevant truncations remain incompletely defined. Here, we show that thrombin, a serine protease associated with inflammatory conditions, selectively cleaves Syn at Lys6–Gly7, generating a 7–140 fragment despite the presence of multiple potential cleavage sites. Cleavage is modulated by ionic strength and the conformational ensemble of Syn, with more extended states being preferentially cleaved. The resulting 7–140 fragment adopts a more compact conformational ensemble, delays the formation of aggregation-prone species, produces fibrils with altered morphology and shows reduced membrane-induced α-helix formation. Although 7–140 aggregates are modestly less toxic, the truncation also impairs physiological functions of the protein. These findings describe a mechanism by which an inflammation-associated protease, thrombin, may contribute to Parkinson’s disease by selectively modifying Syn structure, aggregation and function.

articles.title: Nonlinear responses induced by inhomogeneous edge states in a centrosymmetric topological insulator
A human erythropoietin-albumin fusion protein tailored for enhanced plasma half-life and delivery across mucosal surfaces
articles.abstract: Abstract Erythropoietin (EPO) products stimulate production of erythrocytes in patients with anemia. The drugs are delivered intravenously or subcutaneously up to several times per week due to short plasma half-life. Improving the pharmacokinetic properties of EPO will allow less frequent administration, and thus impact therapeutic utility and patient compliance. In this study, we took advantage of an albumin variant (QMP) engineered for improved engagement of FcRn, a key regulator of the plasma half-life of albumin. After genetic coupling of EPO to QMP, the fusion protein shows favorable neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) binding, and 5.2-fold prolonged plasma half-life in human FcRn expressing mice upon intravenous administration, when comparing with EPO fused to WT albumin, with a similar half-life obtained following subcutaneous administration. Importantly, both fusions bind the EPO receptor with binding kinetics equal to that of the product darbepoetin alfa. After intravenous administration, mice receiving darbepoetin alfa experiences a faster drop in EPO levels compared to those given EPO-QMP, and moreover, we measure a prolonged increase in erythrocytes with EPO-QMP. Furthermore, intranasal administration results in 5-fold higher circulating amounts of EPO-QMP and a prolonged increase in erythrocytes compared to darbepoetin alfa. Thus, long-acting EPO-QMP could be an attractive design to explore for both invasive and non-invasive delivery to patients with anemia.

articles.title: Updated global estimates of carbon burial in seagrass sediments
Detector-mediated cross-spectral prediction with a gate-tunable van der Waals tunneling photodetector
articles.abstract: Abstract Cross-spectral prediction infers information in one spectral band from observations acquired in another. This task is ill-posed because multiple target-band signals can be compatible with a single source observation. Image-space supervision alone does not test consistency with a measured detector response. Here, we incorporate the calibrated response manifold of a gate-tunable PdSe 2 /h-BN/WSe 2 photodetector as a differentiable detector-response layer. Parameterized by wavelength, optical power, source-drain bias and gate voltage, this layer constrains the magnitude and polarity of the predicted detector response while preserving image fidelity. In visible-to-infrared cross-spectral prediction, the framework achieves a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 26.58 dB and a structural similarity index of 0.89. It also reduces detector-space error relative to architecture-only and response-corrupted controls. Post-inference measurements further evaluate 64-mask response consistency after 1310 nm optical re-encoding. These results establish detector-mediated cross-spectral prediction as a framework that combines image reconstruction with measured response-space consistency under the tested conditions.

articles.title: Genetic mechanisms underlying the associations between brain structure and mental health
Statistical inference of keystone taxa reshaping the assembly rules of forest root microbiomes
articles.abstract: Abstract Root-associated fungi and bacteria play pivotal roles in terrestrial ecosystem processes. However, identifying keystone taxa driving below-ground microbial assembly remains a major challenge. Here, we present a statistical framework for identifying microbes that reorganize microbiome assembly. Using 1,270 root samples collected from a cool-temperate forest in Japan, we reconstruct assembly landscapes describing the probabilistic structure of community states. We then find that several endophytic fungi (e.g., Phialocephala and Oidiodendron ) are strongly associated with the reorganization of assembly landscape topography along abundance gradients, coinciding with shifts in mycorrhizal symbiosis. Independent datasets from Europe confirm that the highlighted genera are significantly associated with changes in mycorrhizal colonization patterns. Prokaryotic communities exhibit transitions among states characterized by core taxa, Pseudomonadota, or Actinomycetota, strongly associated with abundance gradients of Candidatus Udaeobacter and several endophytic fungi. These findings provide a scalable framework for prioritizing candidate keystone taxa and linking microbiome assembly to ecosystem-scale processes.

articles.title: Construction of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues through palladium/norbornene catalysis
Biomimetic hydrophobic gating in MXene polypyrrole–based artificial Ion channels for efficient perchlorate sensing
articles.abstract: Abstract Ion selective electrodes represent a promising approach for ion detection based on potentiometric sensing principle. However, their practical application is often hampered by insufficient selectivity, primarily caused by interference from structurally similar ions. Herein, inspired by biological potassium ion channels, we demonstrate an efficient perchlorate ion selective electrode via the self–assembly of pyrrole–functionalized MXene nanosheets and methylated quaternary ammonium compounds. The resulting composite sensor significantly outperforms commercial ion selective electrodes with a > 10 4 –fold lower detection limit (10 –9.7 M), 18–fold higher selectivity ( K ij of 130.4), and a maximum sensitivity up to 59.6 mV/dec for perchlorate. Synchrotron X–ray scattering and mechanistic studies attribute this superior performance to a hydrophobic gating mechanism arising from dehydration effects and transport resistance within confined channels, which effectively lowers the energy barrier for perchlorate transport by 12.13 kcal/mol compared to that of sulfate. Furthermore, the sensor was optimized via substituent engineering for broad-spectrum anion detection and integrated into a portable platform for continuous on–site monitoring, achieving accuracy comparable to ion chromatography in real–world scenarios.

articles.title: Orbital engineering of asymmetric Cu sites in MOFs for fenton reaction towards atomic surface manufacturing
Early-life bovine respiratory virome analysis reveals phage-driven adaptation and cross-host evolutionary signatures
articles.abstract: Abstract Past outbreaks of zoonotic viral infections highlight the importance of understanding respiratory virome ecology. As major food-producing animals with frequent human contact, cattle represent a critical host at the human-animal interface; however, the early-life establishment of their respiratory virome and its evolutionary connections to viruses from other hosts remain underexplored. Here, we longitudinally profile the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using an optimized viral enrichment procedure and metagenomic workflow. Viral communities exhibited increased richness and turnover, reflecting ecological structuring during early life. Temperate phages dominate the URT phage community and share virulence- and mobility-associated genes with bacterial hosts, likely contributing to host adaptation and colonization persistence. Vertebrate-associated viruses emerge after the first week of life. Targeted reassembly from bovine URT viromes recovers near-complete betacoronavirus-like (CoV-D180) and adenovirus-like (AdV-D56) genomes positioned phylogenetically between bovine and human viral lineages. Competitive mapping of bovine-derived CoV-D180 and AdV-D56 to human respiratory metatranscriptomic datasets reveals genome-specific, regionally structured coverage patterns distinct from reference viruses, supporting shared sequence features in conserved genomic regions across host-associated viral lineages. Collectively, these findings reveal early-life assembly dynamics of the bovine respiratory virome and highlight cross-host signatures in a One Health framework.

articles.title: The integrated environmental zoning-based regulation further enhances sustainable development in China
Oncogenic modulation of MAPK signaling in leukemia via SPNS2-driven sphingolipid metabolism and membrane nanodomains remodeling
articles.abstract: Abstract Lipid metabolism rewiring is an essential determinant of cancer progression, yet the key metabolic checkpoints which govern this process remain poorly defined. Using functional genomics in a mouse model of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), we identify the sphingosine-1-phosphate transporter SPNS2 as a critical sphingolipid checkpoint protein which modulates leukemia progression. SPNS2 expression is regulated by MYC and progressively declines during AML differentiation, highlighting its tumor-suppressive role in a subset of Core Binding Factor AMLs. By integrating steady-state and serine isotope-tracing lipidomics, RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and high-resolution microscopy, with gain- and loss-of-function approaches, we show that SPNS2 modulation rewires sphingolipid metabolism by modifying sphingomyelin abundance. This remodeling alters membrane nanodomain organization, active RAS localization, and MAPK signaling. Exogenous reintroduction of SPNS2 decreases sphingomyelin levels, disrupts nanodomain organization, and limits leukemic progression in various AML mouse models. We further reveal in a cohort of patients with AML that low SPNS2 expression is associated with increased sensitivity to MAPK pathway inhibition, and demonstrate functionally in vivo that SPNS2 silencing sensitizes AML cells to MEK1/2 inhibition. Collectively, our data reveal a mechanism by which sphingolipid transport dynamics intersect with oncogenic signaling to control cancer progression.

articles.title: Computational modeling and preclinical evaluation support targeting somatic instability for Huntington’s disease treatment
Lipid stoichiometry and biomarkers reflect microbial acclimation and nutrient stress across the Atlantic Ocean
Integrated on-chip quantum light sources on a van der Waals platform
Concentration quenching resistant violet-blue TADF OLEDs via indirect conformal distributions tuning in solid-state
articles.abstract: Abstract Controlling conformation distributions is the key to manipulate material properties of multi-conformal molecules. Distinct from previous strategy with direct change or impact on the flexible groups, we tune the conformation distribution through changing peripheral groups to influence their intermolecular interactions. Two blue violet TADF emitters, namely tert -butyl substituted 5-(2,12-di-tert-butyl-5,9-dioxa-13b-boranaphtho[3,2,1-de]anthracen-7-yl)−10,10-diphenyl-5,10-dihydrodibenzo[b,e][1,4]azagermine (TDBA-PAG) and cumenyl substituted 5-(2,12-bis(2-phenylpropan-2-yl)−5,9-dioxa-13b-boranaphtho[3,2,1-de]anthracen-7-yl)−10,10-diphenyl-5,10-dihydrodibenzo[b,e][1,4]azagermine (TPDBA-PAG) were designed and synthesized. With the same germanium-integrated donor, the two compounds show similar emission properties in solution with calculated conformation dominantly of their quasi-axial (QA) forms (> 97%). However, TPDBA-PAG presents a lower QA ratio compared with TDBA-PAG, which endows the former with more pronounced TADF emission, higher emission efficiency and reduced concentration quenching phenomena in solid state. As a result, TPDBA-PAG performed as one of the best non-doped and doped violet-blue emitters and successfully sensitized MesB-DIDOBNA-N to achieve record high EQE max of 24.7% at 406 nm, making significant progress in NUV OLEDs.

articles.title: Strand- and replication timing-dependent functions of DNA polymerase η in human DNA replication
Supervising the search process produces reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents
articles.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are transforming web search by shifting from document ranking to synthesizing answers, and are increasingly deployed as autonomous agentic search systems that iteratively interact with external knowledge sources. Despite this progress, building effective search agents remains challenging because high-quality intermediate search steps are difficult to generate. Previous approaches have primarily relied on outcome supervision, rewarding agents only for producing correct final answers. This often leads to reward hacking and excessive dependence on parametric memory, limiting generalization to out-of-domain tasks. To address these limitations, we introduce RAG-Gym, a framework that shifts supervision from final answers to the search process itself. With RAG-Gym, we systematically investigate architecture design, parameter optimization, and action evaluation, identifying reasoning reflection as a critical capability for search agents. Building on this insight, we propose Re 2 Search++, a process-supervised agent that achieves substantial improvements on multi-hop information-seeking benchmarks, especially in out-of-domain settings. Performance gains are driven primarily by higher-quality search queries rather than answer optimization alone, and the learned search critics transfer across models, including proprietary LLMs. These findings show that supervising the search process produces more reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents.

articles.title:
Mapping
the Carbon Footprint of Organic Chemicals
in Commerce
articles.abstract: Abstract The chemical industry is a major contributor to global CO2 emissions, accounting for ∼10% of total greenhouse gases, underscoring the need for a sustainability transition. However, public carbon footprint data exists for only hundreds of the more than 100,000 chemicals in commerce, limiting effective action. To address this, we collect high-quality primary chemical carbon footprint data and refine a machine learning model to estimate the carbon footprint of 94,697 chemicals in commerce across 26 national and regional chemical inventories. Our analysis reveals clear molecular structure–carbon footprint relationships that may guide future molecular design: carbon footprints are strongly linked to molecular frameworks, the number of ring structures, and types of heteroatoms. Newly commercialized chemicals tend to have higher carbon footprints than older chemicals, emphasizing the urgent need to embed “sustainable-by-design” principles into chemical innovation from the outset. This study provides a database of chemical carbon footprints and actionable insights for the sustainable design and use of chemicals, supporting the environmental decision-making of chemical producers, consumers, and policymakers.

articles.title:
Longitudinal
Multiomics Reveals Core Microbiome Disruption
and Potential Keystone-Associated Recovery Following Pesticide Exposure
articles.abstract: Abstract Pesticides have become indispensable in modern agriculture, serving as a primary tool to minimize crop loss amid increasing human population pressures. While the negative effects of pesticides on the soil microbiome have been reported, the temporal dynamics of soil microorganisms under pesticide use remain underexplored. Specifically, limited knowledge exists regarding how the soil microbiome responds to pesticides before and after the manufacturer-labeled ‘safe period’ of 21 days after application. We conducted a longitudinal microcosm study to investigate the temporal impacts of herbicide, fungicide, and insecticide on soil microbial diversity, composition, network complexity, and functional pathways across five time points. Our results show that soil microbial communities are negatively impacted by pesticide applications, but there is a trend of recovery after 21 days. We found a significant impact of the temporal persistence of pesticides on both bacterial and fungal community composition, with a stronger effect on fungi. Network analysis revealed that core microbiome networks were negatively impacted by pesticide applications, with the core microbial nodes, raw associations, and modularity declining in pesticide-treated soils, and this negative effect was particularly strong for pyrethroid insecticides. We identified several differentially abundant taxa, including Xanthobacteraceae and Vicinamibacteriales among bacteria, and Mortierella, Mytilinidales among fungi, which could serve as useful biomarkers for pesticide-affected soils. Results from microbial co-occurrence network analysis revealed that one ASV assigned to the Methyloligellaceae family consistently emerged as a keystone taxon in pesticide-treated soils. Using genome-resolved metagenomics, we assembled the genomes (MAGs) of Methyloligellaceae members and found these taxa harbor putative genes associated with pesticide degradation and antimicrobial resistance, suggesting their possible role in community recovery. Given the remarkably dynamic nature of soil microbial communities, our findings bridge an important knowledge gap regarding the short-term dynamics of microbial structures and functional pathways in response to major pesticides.

articles.title:
Solar
Activation of Peroxymonosulfate by Chromophoric
Dissolved Organic Matter Enables Predictable Micropollutant Attenuation
in Real Waters
articles.abstract: Abstract Solar-driven activation of peroxymonosulfate (PMS) is a promising advanced oxidation process for water and wastewater treatment; however, the kinetics of emerging contaminant removal in real water matrices remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated PMS photosensitization in three environmentally relevant water matrices and evaluated its role in the abatement of 42 pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs). Under simulated solar irradiation, CDOM promoted PMS transformation and generated multiple photochemically produced reactive intermediates (PPRIs). A multiple-probe chemical method was employed to quantify the cumulative exposure doses of HO•, SO4•–, Cl2•–, CO3•–, and 1O2. Across the tested matrices, PPRI exposure doses followed the order CO3•– > 1O2 > Cl2•– ∼ SO4•– > HO•. The measured PPRI exposure doses, together with second-order rate constants, reasonably predicted PPCP removal in the solar/PMS/CDOM system. For several phenolic and aniline-containing PPCPs, DOM-mediated inhibition was observed and was attributed to reductive back-reaction of one-electron oxidation intermediates; incorporating inhibition factors improved the agreement between calculated and experimental removal efficiencies. Furthermore, four commonly detected PPCPs, sucralose, metformin, caffeine, and carbamazepine, were first identified as practical indicator compounds for estimating PPRI exposure without adding external probe chemicals. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for predicting PPCP attenuation during solar/PMS treatment in CDOM-rich waters and highlight the importance of secondary radicals in real aquatic matrices.

articles.title: Multiheme c -Type Cytochrome-Dependent Arsenate Reduction Enhances Methanogenesis in Methanosarcina acetivorans
articles.abstract: Abstract Microorganism-mediated arsenate (As(V)) reduction plays a critical role in arsenic mobility and microbial adaptation in arsenic-contaminated anoxic environments. Current understanding of microbial As(V) reduction has primarily focused on two pathways: extracellular reduction mediated by membrane-bound As(V) respiratory reductase, and intracellular reduction catalyzed by cytoplasmic As(V) detoxification reductase. Here, we report an extracellular As(V) reduction process that operates independently of both known As(V) reductases and is mediated by methanogenic archaea that are recognized for obligate methanogenesis across diverse anoxic habitats. We demonstrate that a model methanogenic archaeon is capable of concurrently performing intracellular methanogenesis and extracellular As(V) reduction, with the latter process significantly enhancing methanogenic growth. Through a combination of microbial physiological, biochemical, and molecular genetic approaches, we identify multiheme c-type cytochromes (MHCs), which are widely distributed within the order Methanosarcinales and have been previously implicated in extracellular iron reduction, as the key molecular components responsible for extracellular As(V) reduction. Furthermore, employing density functional theory simulations, we propose plausible reduction pathways for As(V) reduction mediated by the heme prosthetic groups of MHCs and confirm their thermodynamic feasibility. This work not only provides new insights into the previously overlooked coupling between arsenic transformation and methanogenesis in anoxic environments on Earth, but also underscores the interconnected nature of iron and As(V) reduction, both of which can be mediated by MHCs.

articles.title:
Novel NIR-II Imaging
Reveals Gut-First, Brain-Later
Inorganic Mercury Signals with Structural Injury in Zebrafish
articles.abstract: Abstract Mercury (Hg) neurotoxicity has generally been assessed by organic methylmercury, whereas inorganic mercury [Hg(II)] is often considered less likely to cause direct brain exposure. Conventional approaches cannot resolve the in vivo spatiotemporal distribution of Hg(II) across tissues. In this study, we first developed an Hg(II)-responsive aggregation-induced emission sensor for second near-infrared (NIR-II) fluorescence imaging, which was then employed to track Hg(II) signals in live zebrafish. The sensor produced enhanced NIR-II signals in the presence of Hg(II), allowing low-background, noninvasive, and real-time imaging. We observed that Hg(II)-responsive sensor signals first appeared in the intestinal region and later increased in the brain region, revealing an intestine-first and brain-later temporal pattern in living zebrafish. During a 48-h continuous exposure followed by depuration, brain-region Hg(II)-responsive sensor fluorescence increased with exposure concentration and time and remained detectable during the depuration phase. Expansion microscopy further showed that low-dose Hg(II) exposure reduced the brain cell density and average cell size, and disrupted the local tissue organization. These results provided in vivo evidence of Hg(II)-responsive sensor in the brain region and its association with structural brain injury during development. Thus, inorganic Hg should also be considered in the assessments of developmental brain exposure and neural structural injury.

articles.title:
Influence of Urban
Form, Weather and Population on
Outdoor Airborne Infection Risk: Implications in Greater London for
SARS-CoV-2
articles.abstract: Abstract Although airborne infectious disease transmission outdoors is possible, particularly in densely built urban areas with limited ventilation, the role of urban morphology and neighborhood climate heterogeneity in modulating the risk remains poorly quantified. We couple an urban climate model (SUEWS) and a modified Wells-Riley framework to develop a transferable neighborhood-scale approach for mapping outdoor airborne infection risk across morphologically diverse neighborhoods, factoring in urban form, population distribution and meteorologically driven viral infectivity decay. We demonstrate this framework by applying it to SARS-CoV-2 in Greater London. Considering outdoor urban ventilation alone, estimated risk follows a diurnal cycle and peaks at night. Including population distribution, daytime risk in busy commercial centers is up to 7.23 times higher than nighttime. Infectivity decay from ultraviolet B (UVB) exposure reduces risk by 35–45% in less dense areas and up to 99% in high built-density neighborhoods. Despite this mitigation, the highest risks persist in high-rise, high-workplace-density districts (e.g., City of London and Westminster), while lower-rise areas (e.g., Lambeth and Croydon) exhibit reductions exceeding 90%. For SARS-CoV-2, these findings demonstrate strong intraurban heterogeneity in outdoor airborne infection risk in Greater London. More broadly, the transferable framework supports high-resolution mapping to inform targeted, place-based public health interventions.

articles.title: Issue Editorial Masthead

Event-Scale Deposition
of Atmospheric Microplastics
in Snowfall of the Sierra Nevada in North America
articles.abstract: Abstract Atmospheric deposition of microplastics (MPs) at an event-scale resolution can be measured in snowfall events, as snow scavenges atmospheric MPs and the snowpack serves as a repository for MP accumulation. We monitored MP deposition in freshly fallen snow, the snowpack, and dry deposition over the course of 6 months in the Sierra Nevada of North America. Average microplastic concentrations in fresh snow ranged from 11.8 to 37.5 p/L at remote sites, which were significantly less than the 68.3 to 92.9 p/L MP concentrations found at the anthropogenically impacted site. Average bulk deposition rates were estimated to be 267 to 3190 p/m2/day at remote sites, significantly lower than the 3242 to 7480 p/m2/day at the anthropogenically impacted site. HYSPLIT back-trajectory modeling characterized the potential regional transport of MPs from upwind regions that were predominantly agricultural and suburban areas, as well as localized anthropogenic activities that could significantly affect MP deposition rates in snowfall. This study introduces high-throughput FTIR analysis methods with a highlight on fiber spectroscopy, demonstrates the value of estimating MP fluxes at the meteorological event scale, reports MP deposition rates in a critical water resource, and provides a basis for future long-term atmospheric MP monitoring.

articles.title: Issue Publication Information

Soil
Heating from
Fire Induces Bidirectional Changes
in Dissolved Organic Matter Release and Organic Sulfur Speciation
articles.abstract: Abstract Soil heating from fire influences dissolved organic matter (DOM) release but has unknown effects on organic sulfur (S) speciation, with implications for S and metal cycling in aquatic environments. Here, low and high organic carbon soils (4.80 versus 50.4%) were heated at environmentally relevant temperatures and durations (75–300 °C, 0.25–4.0 h) and subject to leaching experiments that quantified DOM and inorganic anion release, and changes in organic S speciation via S X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy. In both soils, heating between 75 and 200 °C increased dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and inorganic sulfate (SO42–) release (by up to 24- and 88-fold, respectively) while decreasing the % highly reduced S in DOM (e.g., thiols), indicating thiol oxidation to SO42–. Soil heating at 300 °C decreased DOC release and increased SO42– release, with step increases in DOM aromaticity and % heterocyclic reduced S species (e.g., thiophenes). Across treatments, DOM aromaticity positively correlated with DOM % heterocyclic reduced S, interpreted to reflect organic S cyclization during heating. The observed bidirectional changes in organic S speciation in DOM due to soil heating, with thiol oxidation at ≤200 °C and S cyclization at 300 °C with SO42– releases, provide mechanistic insights that improve the prediction of fire effects on S, C, and metal cycling in aquatic environments.

articles.title:
Substantial
Emerging Impact of Amine-Based Carbon
Capture on Atmospheric Particle Formation under Carbon Neutrality
articles.abstract: Abstract Carbon capture (CC) is indispensable to carbon neutrality, and amine-based absorption using monoethanolamine (MEA) is among the most mature CC technologies. MEA can enhance atmospheric new particle formation (NPF), the primary source of atmospheric particles. However, the atmospheric impacts of MEA escaping from future large-scale CC deployment remain unknown. Here, we develop a three-dimensional model that represents MEA sources, sinks, and H2SO4-MEA nucleation based on quantum chemical and cluster dynamics calculations, to evaluate atmospheric MEA and its impacts from CC deployment at China’s coal-fired power plants under carbon-neutrality scenarios. By 2060, even moderate CC deployment raises atmospheric MEA concentrations to tens of pptv, exceeding dimethylamine (DMA), the canonical urban NPF agent. H2SO4-MEA nucleation consequently overtakes H2SO4-DMA nucleation across extensive CC-deployment regions (∼1 million km2) and is more than 10 times stronger within the CC-intensive core (∼0.2 million km2), raising particle number concentrations by 50–187% and exposing ∼430 million people to levels exceeding the WHO high-exposure benchmark. The associated rise in ultrafine particles is estimated to cause ∼34,800 additional deaths across China in 2060. We reveal that CC deployment may deliver climate benefits while inadvertently worsening particulate pollution and public-health burdens, warranting proactive and early preventive action.

articles.title:
Correction to “Nitrous
Oxide Emissions from
Urban Green Spaces Substantially Offset Their Carbon Sequestration
Benefits”

Recombinase Polymerase
Amplification Coupled with
Graphene Oxide Nanomaterial-Assisted Purification and Target Signal
Selection for Highly Sensitive and Rapid Harmful Algae Detection
articles.abstract: Abstract Harmful algal blooms (HABs) pose serious ecological and health risks, creating an urgent need for rapid, sensitive, and accurate detection of harmful algae. Here, we developed a graphene oxide (GO)- and Mg2+-regulated recombinase polymerase amplification assay (G-M-RPA) for rapid and ultrasensitive detection of Heterosigma akashiwo, Prorocentrum minimum, and Akashiwo sanguinea. Using conserved internal transcribed spacer sequences, we designed species-specific primers labeled with 6-carboxyfluorescein for fluorescence readout. Innovative one-step purification of RPA products was achieved using self-synthesized GO-wrapped magnetic nanocomposites instead of traditional purification kits, reducing purification time from 15 to 2 min (∼86.7%). The fluorescence resonance energy transfer property of the GO nanosheets was applied to quench the fluorescence of excess single-stranded primers, significantly lowering background levels. Mg2+ further enhanced primer–GO interactions, likely through electrostatic screening and Mg2+-mediated interactions. The entire detection process was completed within ∼30 min, achieving a genomic DNA detection limit of 3.3 fg/μL, corresponding to ∼7 cells/mL for H. akashiwo. The assay also showed reliable performance in mixed-DNA and seawater matrices, with favorable reproducibility and short-term stability. Overall, the proposed G-M-RPA strategy provides a rapid, sensitive, and practical platform for multispecies harmful-algae detection, nearshore environmental monitoring, and early warning of HABs.

articles.title:
Biochar
Application Enhances Photochemical Reactivity
of Dissolved Organic Matter to Stimulate CO2 Emissions
in Paddy Water
articles.abstract: Abstract Dissolved organic matter (DOM) plays a pivotal role in regulating photochemical reactivity and carbon turnover in flooded paddy systems. While biochar (BC) is recognized as a promising strategy for soil carbon preservation, its impact on DOM evolution and photochemical carbon cycle in paddy water remains unknown. Here, we demonstrated that BC amendment continuously enhanced the photogeneration of hydroxyl radicals (•OH) and low-energy excited triplet-state DOM (3DOM*-L) in paddy water, increasing CO2 emissions by an average of 35.5% while playing a minor role in CH4 formation over a 34-day incubation. The enhanced photoactivity was associated with the enrichment of the photoactive molecular pool characterized by highly aromatic compounds and polyphenols with higher aromaticity, unsaturation, and oxygenated degrees. The proposed mechanisms in enriching photoactive DOM of paddy water depended on soil types, i.e., BC facilitated the biotic reprocessing of inert, highly recalcitrant aromatics into metabolites associated with photoactivity in sandy soil, whereas abiotic processes, including BC-induced dissolved black carbon release and mineral-associated organic carbon desorption, likely played more important roles in loam soil. Enhanced anaerobic fermentation further supplied photolabile substrates for amplifying mineralization. Extrapolation estimations suggested that BC-enhanced photochemistry may release an additional 3.56–15.47 Tg CO2 yr–1 globally, potentially offsetting ∼0.7–7.0% of BC’s CO2 mitigation potential. The findings revealed a previously unrecognized photochemical pathway of BC-involved carbon loss across the soil-water continuum, with implications for evaluating the net climate benefit of biochar as a carbon management strategy.

articles.title:
Modeling
to Plan the Future Cities We Desire

Observation-Based
Emission Estimates of the Potent
Greenhouse Gas HFC-23 for Article 5 and Non-Article 5 Country Groups
under the Montreal Protocol
articles.abstract: Abstract The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol requires parties to destroy, to the extent practicable, HFC-23 generated as a byproduct during the production of controlled hydrochlorofluorocarbons and hydrofluorocarbons. Global total HFC-23 emissions estimated from reported abatement and known sources (bottom-up) agreed with those inferred from atmospheric observations (top-down) before 2015, but have been substantially lower since then. Here, we show that during 2011–2013, bottom-up estimates of global total HFC-23 emissions were right for the wrong reasons: bottom-up estimates for the non-Article 5 (mainly developed) country group were lower than top-down estimates (1.7 ± 0.2 vs 3.1 ± 0.5 Gg yr–1 on average), while those for the Article 5 (mainly developing) country group were higher (11.8 ± 0.4 vs 9.7 ± 1.0 Gg yr–1), resulting in a cancellation at the global scale. We further show that during 2015–2023, while the underestimation of global bottom-up emissions was dominated by the Article 5 country group, the non-Article 5 country group also contributed in 2023 [bottom-up (byproduct emissions reported to UNEP plus other known sources) vs top-down: 0.5 ± 0.2 vs 1.3 ± 0.6 Gg yr–1]. Our results underscore improvement of emission accounting and mitigation for both country groups under the Kigali Amendment.

articles.title:
Mn(II)-Mediated
Abiotic Humification via Synergistic
Interactions with Molecular Oxygen
articles.abstract: Abstract Terrestrial organic carbon (OC) dynamics critically influence the global carbon budget. Humification is a key pathway for stabilizing OC by transforming labile compounds into macromolecular polymers. High-valent manganese oxides (e.g., Mn(IV)O2) are well-known as efficient catalysts of abiotic humification, whereas the role of Mn(II) in OC transformation remains poorly understood. Here, dissolved Mn2+ drives oxidative polymerization and nitrogen-enriched humic-like product formation in the presence of common soil precursors─catechol, glycine, and glucose─through a synergistic interaction with molecular oxygen (O2). Mechanistically, Mn2+ mediates sequential single-electron transfers from catechol to O2, forming reactive intermediates that potentially couple with Maillard precursors to yield nitrogen-enriched macromolecules. FT-ICR-MS reveals that CHON species in lignin-like and highly condensed aromatic regions collectively account for 75.6% of total product relative abundance. This process is accompanied by the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which could further enhance molecular diversity. Across 14 soil and freshwater DOM samples, 13.1–54.7% of assigned product formulas overlap with those in the corresponding DOM samples. Collectively, these shared formulas account for 78% of the total relative abundance of product formulas, indicating molecular-formula-level compositional similarity. These findings provide mechanistic and molecular-level insight into the underexplored role of Mn2+ in abiotic humification.

articles.title:
Suspect
and Non-Targeted
Analysis of Organophosphate
Esters in Plastic Consumer Products via Ion Mobility Spectrometry-Mass
Spectrometry
articles.abstract: Abstract Organophosphate esters (OPEs) are widely used as plasticizers and flame retardants in plastic products, posing critical environmental and human health risks. Traditional liquid chromatography-high resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) approaches face trade-offs between comprehensive coverage and spectral purity. This study established an advanced multidimensional identification framework utilizing LC coupled with cyclic ion mobility spectrometry and quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (LC-cIMS-QTOF). An integrated screening workflow merging targeted analysis, suspect screening, and nontargeted analysis (NTA) was deployed to characterize the OPEs in consumer plastics. A total of 63 OPEs were successfully characterized across seven polymer types, with 10, 22, and 31 compounds identified via targeted, suspect, and NTA workflows, respectively. Notably, 14 OPEs were traced back to the transformation products of phosphite antioxidants, ethoxy-linked OPEs constituted another predominant class with 22 congeners. This comprehensive characterization enriches current knowledge regarding the diversity of OPEs within plastic products, providing critical target lists for future migration and exposure assessments. Methodologically, the benefits of IMS, including providing cleaner mass spectra, discriminating isomers, and improving confidence levels, were demonstrated throughout the OPEs identification workflow. This established multidimensional screening strategy serves as a robust and efficient tool for uncovering OPEs contaminants in both plastic matrices and broader environmental media.

articles.title:
Celebrating the
30th Anniversary of the Department
of Environmental Science and Engineering, Fudan University

Microplastic-Derived
Dissolved Organic Matter Regulates
Reactive Bromine Species Formation by Modulating the Photochemistry
of Seawater Dissolved Organic Matter
articles.abstract: Abstract Microplastic-derived dissolved organic matter (MP-DOM) is emerging as a non-negligible organic input to marine systems, yet how its interactions with seawater DOM (S-DOM) regulate the photochemical formation of reactive bromine species (RBS) remains unclear. In this study, the RBS formation potential of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC)-derived MP-DOM, S-DOM, and their mixed systems was systematically investigated under simulated solar irradiation. MP-DOM input exerted a nonlinear ratio-dependent regulatory effect on S-DOM-mediated RBS formation. At relatively low MP-DOM proportions (5–20%), the formation rate constant of 4-bromo-3,5-dimethyl-1H-pyrazole (Br-DMPZ), which represents the RBS formation potential, increased relative to S-DOM alone, reaching a maximum enhancement of 47.4% at 20% MP-DOM under seawater halide ion conditions (540 mM Cl– + 0.8 mM Br–). This enhancement was associated with increased quinone-/carbonyl-related redox-active structures, electron exchange capacity, and tannin-like components, which could facilitate photoinduced charge separation, electron transfer, and Br– oxidation. In contrast, higher MP-DOM proportions (40–50%) promoted hydrophobic lipid-like mixed assemblies, enhancing excited-state quenching and suppressing electron transfer and RBS photogeneration. These findings demonstrate that MP-DOM is not an inert byproduct of microplastic aging but rather an important regulatory factor in S-DOM-mediated halogen photochemistry in plastic-impacted marine waters.
